proposal.title: Kalquelruk: a conformance suite for calendar sharing
proposal.summary: Kalquelruk builds a conformance suite for calendar sharing for people who schedule across organisations.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.text: Calendar invitations break silently between different servers. People who schedule across organisations depend on calendar interoperability every day, yet the tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

sections.heading: Approach
sections.text: We will build a conformance suite for calendar sharing called Kalquelruk. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Each component gets tests and a fuzz target before it is merged.

sections.heading: Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
sections.text: Calendar interoperability is part of the Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

sections.heading: Deliverables and licence
sections.text: All code will be released under the GPL-3.0-or-later licence in http://forge.test/kalquelruk/kalquelruk. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

sections.heading: Milestones
sections.text: The work runs over 11 months in 4 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 3. Core implementation ends in month 5. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 8. Documentation and release ends in month 11.

sections.heading: Budget justification
sections.text: The plan asks for 55350.00 EUR for 77 days of work over 4 tasks. Day rates range from 650.00 EUR to 750.00 EUR.

proposal.narrative:
Problem
Calendar invitations break silently between different servers. People who schedule across organisations depend on calendar interoperability every day, yet the tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

Approach
We will build a conformance suite for calendar sharing called Kalquelruk. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Each component gets tests and a fuzz target before it is merged.

Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
Calendar interoperability is part of the Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

Deliverables and licence
All code will be released under the GPL-3.0-or-later licence in http://forge.test/kalquelruk/kalquelruk. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

Milestones
The work runs over 11 months in 4 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 3. Core implementation ends in month 5. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 8. Documentation and release ends in month 11.

Budget justification
